text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on July 31 in history.
1498 - Christopher Columbus, on his third voyage to the New World, discovered an island which he named Trinidad.
1556 - Saint Ignatius of Loyola, Spanish soldier and priest who founded the Society of Jesus (the Jesuits), died.
1602 - Charles, Duc de Biron, was executed for conspiring against Henri IV of France.
1812 - A year after declaring independence, Venezuela fell to the Spanish and its leader Francisco de Miranda was arrested.
1875 - Andrew Johnson, the 17th president of the United States (1865-1869), died. He became president following the assassination of Abraham Lincoln.
1886 - Franz Liszt, Hungarian composer and pianist died. Originator of the symphonic poem, he was a prolific teacher and a huge influence on Wagner and Richard Strauss.
1910 - Dr Hawley Crippen, British murderer, was arrested on a ship off Canada. Although disguised, the Captain recognised him and radioed Scotland Yard. This was the first arrest effected by radio.
1912 - Milton Friedman, U.S. economist, Nobel laureate and leading exponent of monetarism, born.
1917 - During the third battle of Ypres, British troops began an advance that dragged on until November with minimal gain.
1919 - The Weimar Constitution was adopted in post-war Germany, establishing a republic. Parliament, which kept the old name of Reichstag, moved to Weimar to avoid association with the Kaiser.
1926 - Afghanistan and the Soviet Union signed a mutual non-agression pact.
1941 - Herman Goering gave a written directive to police chief Reinhard Heydrich to draft a plan for the elimination of European Jews, the "final solution".
1945 - Pierre Laval, prime minister of Vichy France, was captured by the allies in Austria after trying to flee around Europe.
1954 - Mount Godwin-Austen (K2) in the Himalayas was first climbed by an Italian expedition led by Ardito Desio.
1962 - Agreement was reached in principle to expand the Malaya Federation into a wider state called Malaysia within a year.
1964 - U.S. lunar probe Ranger 7 transmitted the first close-up photographs of the moon back to earth.
1964 - Jim Reeves, popular U.S. country music singer, died in an aircrash near Nashville.
1969 - Pope Paul VI visited Uganda, the first time a pontiff had visited Africa.
1971 - On the second day of their moon landing, Apollo 15 astronauts David Scott and James Irwin went for the first ever drive on the moon in their Lunar Roving Vehicle or "moon buggy".

1975 - Former U.S. Teamsters Union President James Hoffa was reported missing. It was believed he had been abducted the previous day and subsequently murdered. He was declared "presumed dead" on December 8, 1982.
1991 - At the end of a two-day summit, Presidents Bush and Gorbachev signed the START treaty cutting their nuclear arsenals.

1992 - A Yak-42 airliner carrying 126 crashed on takeoff from Nanjing airport in east China, killing 106; on the same day a Thai airliner crashed in remote Himalayan foothills, killing all 113 on board.
1993 - King Baudouin of Belgium, Europe's longest serving monarch, died of a heart attack whilst on holiday in Spain.
1994 - The Security Council authorised the use of force in Haiti, clearing the way for a U.S.-led invasion of the country to restore exiled President Jean-Bertrand Aristide to power.

1995 - In a move that took both Hollywood and Wall Street by surprise, the Walt Disney Co. said it would pay $19 billion for Capital Cities/ABC Inc, creating a major force in the entertainment and media industry.
1996 - A group of African leaders agreed to impose full economic sanctions on Burundi after a Tutsi military coup and called for international support.
